heroHeadline: Iran MOU Response Overdue; US Fires on Two Iranian Tankers; Araghchi: 'Reckless Military Adventure' — Day 71
heroSubtitle: Day 71 (May 9): Iran failed to deliver its formal MOU response despite Rubio's May 8 deadline. FM Araghchi accused Washington of 'opting for a reckless military adventure every time a diplomatic solution is on the table.' Iran's semi-official Tasnim called the US MOU terms 'maximalist and unacceptable.' Fox News published satellite imagery allegedly showing a secret Iranian nuclear weapons site ('Rainbow Site,' Semnan) — Araghchi dismissed it as 'Israeli-driven propaganda aimed at disrupting negotiations.' US naval forces fired on two empty Iranian-flagged oil tankers attempting to breach the blockade near the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC's paid-passage scheme for Hormuz — requiring ships to register with the 'Persian Gulf Strait Authority' and pay up to $2M per vessel — continues, but shipowners and insurers remain wary due to mine risks in non-designated lanes. Brent crude fell to ~$101/bbl (down ~7% on the week) on deal optimism and ceasefire affirmations, though markets remain volatile. Approximately 1,600 ships with 23,000 sailors from 87 countries remain stranded in the Persian Gulf. Day 70 (May 8): Iran launched 2 ballistic missiles and 3 drones at UAE — all intercepted; 3 wounded. US and Iran exchanged fire overnight in Hormuz. Trump insisted ceasefire was 'still in effect.' Kalshi markets showed rising deal odds. NBC News: the strait 'will take a long time to reboot.'
